Issued at 226 PM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

This afternoon GOES water vapor imagery and GFS model height 
analysis showed upper level ridging over the central U.S. ahead of 
an upper low that was now over the central California. Surface 
analysis and observations showed high pressure from the U.P. 
northeast into Ontario and Quebec. Under the high a weak pressure 
gradient was continuing to provide light winds to the area. With the 
weak flow, extensive fog that had developed overnight over the 
central and eastern U.P. along with the Keweenaw was taking its time 
dissipating. Most of the fog had lifted into a low stratus deck and 
was now draped from the Menominee and Delta Counties northwest 
towards Marquette and further on to the northern half of Keweenaw. 
The western U.P. avoided much of the fog and thus temperatures had 
warmed mid to upper 60s, while areas under the low clouds remained 
in the 40s. 

Overall it will remain warm through the weekend, with the warmest 
days on Friday and Saturday when highs will be 15-25F above average 
for late October, ranging from the 60s far east to the mid 70s west, 
with even a few locations pushing the upper 70s. Record highs from 
locations with longer historical records are generally in the upper 
70s to low 80s, thus high temperatures could come within 2-5F of the 
records.

The surface high pressure will push east tonight as low pressure 
deepens in the lee of the Rockies, helping to bring southerly flow, 
though still light, into the U.P. This will help pull moisture back 
north through the area tonight, enhanced by moisture from Lake 
Michigan. With relatively ideal conditions for radiational cooling 
expect fog to redevelop over the central and eastern U.P. Fog will 
become dense at times especially over the central third of the CWA. 
Headlines may be needed for dense fog tonight into Friday morning. 
Commuters should leave themselves extra time to reach their 
destinations. The developing southerly flow will help minimize 
cooling over the far west, while the central and east see limited 
cooling once the fog forms. Low temperatures will be a bit warmer 
tonight than previous nights.

Fog will lift on Friday morning with a warm day in store for the 
U.P. as the upper level ridge moves overhead and 850mb temperatures 
warm into the 10-13C range. Expect high temperatures in the 60s east 
to the mid 70s west, and even upper 70s over Ontonagon County and 
southern Houghton County. Dry weather will persist with south winds 
gusting to around 15 mph. 

Saturday will be continued warm but also become windy. Low pressure 
tracking through northern Saskatchewan and into northern Ontario 
will bring a tightening pressure gradient and south winds will 
become gusty, 20-25mph and up to 35mph along the Lake Superior 
shoreline east of Keweenaw Bay. The gusty winds and warm 
temperatures (highs in the 60s and 70s) will bring a heighten 
concerned for fire weather, however, higher dewpoints in the upper 
40s will keep RH over 40% except for parts of Ontonagon and Houghton 
counties were the RH could drop to 35%.

A cold front will sweep across the U.P. from west to east on 
Saturday night bringing a chance for rain showers. Deterministic 
models are trending drier and the chance for 0.1" or more of 
rainfall from the ensembles is only around 10%. Don't expect much in 
the way of rainfall if you do happen to get under one of the 
showers. Winds turn west behind the front and cooler, drier air will 
begin to work into the area through Sunday afternoon. Highs will be 
cooler but still above average, reaching the 50s west and 60s east. 
Humidity will fall as low as 30% over the interior west but winds 
look to remain under 15 mph at this time, limiting fire weather 
concerns. 

High pressure passes east over Ontario and the Great lakes Monday 
and Tuesday favoring dry weather until late Tuesday/Wednesday when 
higher PoPs return. That said, with colder 850mb temps moving 
overhead early next week, delta-Ts maybe sufficient for isolated 
rain showers. Troughing from the west and a resulting sfc low 
pressure mid next week present better (although still low) chances 
for precip, but ensemble guidance quickly diverges on track and 
timing leaving low forecast confidence. The forecast reflects mostly 
slight chance PoPs (14-24%). Otherwise, temps return near normal in 
the wake of the cold front on Sunday peaking in the mid 40s to low 
50s on Monday. Temps Monday night settle into the 20s to mid 30s, 
coldest interior west. A slow warming trend then persists the rest 
of next week.
